doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Wynton Marsalis and the Lincoln Center Orchestra
summary: He feels they play Duke's charts but don't swing; too clean.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Lincoln Center Orchestra. Duke, Duke, Duke, Duke. Ain’t nothing Dukish about what he’s doing as far as I’m concerned. It’s not that — musically they play beautifully. But as far as I’m concerned they don’t swing. Unfortunately I have to put it on the rhythm section. They play the same charts that Duke played, and there’s a world of difference, it’s the personnel.
Sometimes I think it might have something to do with —
It becomes so sterile as far as I’m concerned. It’s too clean.
Too clean, yeah. Too much in the amplification. If you start making the bass too loud it affects the way the music was conceived I think.
